# podnet: manual and documents

The manual is the output of `podnet man --no-pager`.

```text
PODNET(1)                                        podnet 0.4.0-beta.3

NAME
    podnet - Cloudflare tunnels and the WARP client for hosts with strong
    network limits

SYNOPSIS
    podnet COMMAND [OPTIONS]
    podnet man [SECTION] [--no-pager | --roff | --json]

DESCRIPTION
    podnet is one binary for Cloudflare quick tunnels (trycloudflare), named
    tunnels and the Cloudflare WARP client. It is made for hosts with strong
    network limits: no root, no TUN device, no network namespace, no UDP, no
    AF_INET bind, or only TCP 443 out.

    A tunnel reaches the edge with one of four legs: QUIC on UDP 7844, HTTP/2
    on TCP 7844 (directly or through HTTPS_PROXY), QUIC inside a WARP MASQUE
    tunnel on TCP 443, or HTTP/2 through the WebSocket relay on TCP 443
    (--transport relay). With --protocol auto and --transport auto, podnet
    tries the first three in that order.

    podnet pod runs a program with all its traffic sent through a proxy, with
    no LD_PRELOAD (podnet-netns). podnet net gives programs virtual IP
    addresses on a host that refuses AF_INET binds.

    This manual is generated from the command tree of the binary. podnet man
    --roff writes it as a man(7) page, and podnet man --json writes its
    tables.

COMMANDS

    podnet tunnel [OPTIONS]
        Expose a service (cloudflared-style)

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --service-url <SERVICE_URL>
            Quick-tunnel provisioning endpoint. Default:
            https://api.trycloudflare.com.

        --user-agent <USER_AGENT>
            User-Agent sent when provisioning

        --ha-connections <HA_CONNECTIONS>
            Edge connections (1-8), for redundancy: when one is lost, the
            others carry the visitors. The edge chooses the connection of each
            request, and one request uses one connection, so more connections
            do not make one transfer faster. Default: ha-connections of
            --config, else 2

        --protocol <PROTOCOL>
            Edge protocol: quic (UDP 7844), http2 or h2 (TCP 7844), or auto
            (quic, then http2). Default: protocol of --config, else auto.
            Values: auto, quic, http2, h2.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            How to reach the edge: auto (try 7844, fall back to WARP on 443),
            direct (port 7844), warp (carried on TCP 443) or relay (HTTP/2 in
            a WebSocket to the relay of --relay, on TCP 443). Default: auto.
            Values: auto, direct, warp, relay.

        --relay <URL>
            The WebSocket-to-TCP relay of --transport relay: a URL, or a comma
            list of hosts of one deployment. The variable PODNET_RELAY_TOKEN
            (not PODNET_RELAY) gives a token; without it, podnet mints one.
            Default: https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev. Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --warp-identity <PATH>
            Keep the WARP device and MASQUE key here and resume them next run.
            Without it, every run registers a new anonymous device

        --leg-failover <LEG_FAILOVER>
            How the next edge leg starts: staggered (when the leg before has
            not registered in 2 s, or at once when it fails) or serial (only
            after the leg before failed). Default: staggered. Values:
            staggered, serial. Variable: PODNET_LEG_FAILOVER.

        --no-verify
            Do not fetch the public URL to prove reachability. Origin TLS
            checks stay on

        --qr
            Print a QR code for the public URL

        --json
            Print the state of the tunnel as JSON lines on stdout, in place of
            the text lines. Each line is one object with the key "event":
            "ready" (url, tunnel_id, locations, and pin for share) or
            "verified" (url)

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C (it also
            ends the verify of the public URL)

        --auth-user <USER>
            Each visitor must give this user (HTTP Basic), with the password
            of --auth-password-file. A visitor with no right credential gets
            401 and reaches no origin; the origin does not get the header. For
            HTTP origins and --forward (podnet connect --auth-user); not for
            --tcp. Variable: PODNET_AUTH_USER.

        --auth-password-file <FILE>
            The file with the password of --auth-user on its first line (mode
            0600). Variable: PODNET_AUTH_PASSWORD_FILE.

        --check
            Check the plan and stop: the flags, the config file, each origin
            (a connection, and the TLS handshake for https, with no request),
            the files and the directories, and the edge legs. No Cloudflare
            API call, no edge connection, no file is written. Exit 0 when each
            check passes, 1 when a check fails. With --json, one JSON document

        --url <URL>
            HTTP or HTTPS origin. Not with --config

        --unix <UNIX>
            HTTP origin on a unix socket. Not with --config

        --port <PORT>
            HTTP origin on 127.0.0.1:<PORT>. Not with --config

        --tcp <TCP>
            Raw TCP origin. Not with --config

        --forward <FORWARD>
            Expose a raw stream over a WebSocket endpoint (tcp://host:port or
            unix:/path). Not with --config

        --hello-world
            cloudflared's built-in hello world. Not with --config

        --config <CONFIG>
            cloudflared-style YAML config with ingress rules

        --token <TOKEN>
            Named-tunnel token. Prefer the variable TUNNEL_TOKEN or
            --token-file: other users of the host can read a command line.
            Variable: TUNNEL_TOKEN.

        --token-file <PATH>
            Read the named-tunnel token from this file (for example a secret
            of a container). The token is not on the command line. Variable:
            TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE.

        --credentials-file <CREDENTIALS_FILE>
            cloudflared credentials JSON file

        --no-tls-verify
            Skip TLS verification of the origin. Not with --config

        --http-host-header <HTTP_HOST_HEADER>
            Override the Host header sent to the origin. Not with --config

        --strip-accept-encoding
            Drop Accept-Encoding so the origin cannot compress a streaming
            response. Not with --config

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        A quick tunnel in the background: one JSON document with the URL, then
        exit 0.
            $ podnet tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --detach
        A quick tunnel to a local HTTP server.
            $ podnet tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8080
        A quick tunnel to an HTTP server on a unix socket.
            $ podnet tunnel --unix /run/app.sock
        Use the HTTP/2 edge leg on TCP 7844 (no UDP).
            $ podnet tunnel --protocol http2 --url http://127.0.0.1:8080
        Reach the edge through WARP on TCP 443 only.
            $ podnet tunnel --transport warp --hello-world
        A named tunnel.
            $ podnet tunnel --token TOKEN --url http://127.0.0.1:8080
        Ingress rules from a cloudflared configuration file.
            $ podnet tunnel --config config.yml
        Carry a raw stream through the quick tunnel.
            $ podnet tunnel --forward unix:/run/app.sock

    podnet serve [OPTIONS] [DIR]
        Serve a directory over a tunnel

        <DIR>
            Directory to serve

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --service-url <SERVICE_URL>
            Quick-tunnel provisioning endpoint. Default:
            https://api.trycloudflare.com.

        --user-agent <USER_AGENT>
            User-Agent sent when provisioning

        --ha-connections <HA_CONNECTIONS>
            Edge connections (1-8), for redundancy: when one is lost, the
            others carry the visitors. The edge chooses the connection of each
            request, and one request uses one connection, so more connections
            do not make one transfer faster. Default: ha-connections of
            --config, else 2

        --protocol <PROTOCOL>
            Edge protocol: quic (UDP 7844), http2 or h2 (TCP 7844), or auto
            (quic, then http2). Default: protocol of --config, else auto.
            Values: auto, quic, http2, h2.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            How to reach the edge: auto (try 7844, fall back to WARP on 443),
            direct (port 7844), warp (carried on TCP 443) or relay (HTTP/2 in
            a WebSocket to the relay of --relay, on TCP 443). Default: auto.
            Values: auto, direct, warp, relay.

        --relay <URL>
            The WebSocket-to-TCP relay of --transport relay: a URL, or a comma
            list of hosts of one deployment. The variable PODNET_RELAY_TOKEN
            (not PODNET_RELAY) gives a token; without it, podnet mints one.
            Default: https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev. Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --warp-identity <PATH>
            Keep the WARP device and MASQUE key here and resume them next run.
            Without it, every run registers a new anonymous device

        --leg-failover <LEG_FAILOVER>
            How the next edge leg starts: staggered (when the leg before has
            not registered in 2 s, or at once when it fails) or serial (only
            after the leg before failed). Default: staggered. Values:
            staggered, serial. Variable: PODNET_LEG_FAILOVER.

        --no-verify
            Do not fetch the public URL to prove reachability. Origin TLS
            checks stay on

        --qr
            Print a QR code for the public URL

        --json
            Print the state of the tunnel as JSON lines on stdout, in place of
            the text lines. Each line is one object with the key "event":
            "ready" (url, tunnel_id, locations, and pin for share) or
            "verified" (url)

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C (it also
            ends the verify of the public URL)

        --auth-user <USER>
            Each visitor must give this user (HTTP Basic), with the password
            of --auth-password-file. A visitor with no right credential gets
            401 and reaches no origin; the origin does not get the header. For
            HTTP origins and --forward (podnet connect --auth-user); not for
            --tcp. Variable: PODNET_AUTH_USER.

        --auth-password-file <FILE>
            The file with the password of --auth-user on its first line (mode
            0600). Variable: PODNET_AUTH_PASSWORD_FILE.

        --check
            Check the plan and stop: the flags, the config file, each origin
            (a connection, and the TLS handshake for https, with no request),
            the files and the directories, and the edge legs. No Cloudflare
            API call, no edge connection, no file is written. Exit 0 when each
            check passes, 1 when a check fails. With --json, one JSON document

        --dir <DIR>
            Directory to serve (the same as DIR)

        --spa
            Single-page-app fallback to index.html

        --tar
            Give a directory as one tar download: GET /PATH/?tar answers the
            directory PATH as a ustar stream (application/x-tar). Names that
            start with a dot and links out of the directory are left out

        --list
            A directory with no index.html answers a listing of its files:
            HTML, or JSON with the header Accept: application/json. Names that
            start with a dot and links out of the directory are left out

        --upload
            Accept uploads into the directory, for a write user (or the PIN):
            PUT /PATH (curl -T FILE URL/PATH) writes one file, and a multipart
            form POST to a directory adds files. A file goes to its name only
            when it is complete. Names that start with a dot are refused

        --max-upload <BYTES>
            The most bytes of one upload request. A larger request gets 413
            and leaves no file. The Cloudflare edge accepts at most 100 MB in
            one request. Default: 100000000.

        --users <FILE>
            The users of the file server (HTTP Basic), one on each line:
            USER:ROLE:HASH or USER:ROLE:@PASSWORD-FILE. ROLE is read or write.
            HASH comes from --hash-password. The file must have mode 0600.
            Each request must give a user, except a read with --anon-read

        --pin
            Lock the files with a 6-digit PIN, as share --password does.
            podnet prints the PIN. With no --users, the PIN gives the write
            role

        --anon-read
            A GET or HEAD needs no user and no PIN. A change still needs a
            write user

        --hash-password
            Read a password from the first line of stdin, print its hash for
            --users, and exit

        --ingress <INGRESS>
            The road to the visitors: tunnel (the default with no --local),
            relay, or none (the default with --local). --ingress tunnel or
            relay with --local serves the local listeners too. Values: tunnel,
            relay, none.

        --pair <NAME>
            With --ingress relay: the pair name. Default: the pair with the
            most time left; at its expiry the node takes the next stored pair

        --local <ADDR>
            Serve the files on this local listener (more than one is
            permitted): HOST:PORT (or tcp://HOST:PORT), or unix:PATH (mode
            0600). Port 0 takes a free port; podnet prints the bound address.
            A unix socket that answers is refused (exit 69, --replace takes it
            over), a stale socket is removed, a file that is not a socket is
            refused (exit 64). With no --ingress, podnet makes no tunnel

        --token <TOKEN>
            Named-tunnel token. Prefer the variable TUNNEL_TOKEN or
            --token-file: other users of the host can read a command line.
            Variable: TUNNEL_TOKEN.

        --token-file <PATH>
            Read the named-tunnel token from this file (for example a secret
            of a container). The token is not on the command line. Variable:
            TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Serve a directory.
            $ podnet serve --dir ./public
        Serve a directory to this host only, on a local listener. No tunnel.
            $ podnet serve --dir ./public --local 127.0.0.1:8080
        Serve a directory on a unix socket. No tunnel.
            $ podnet serve --dir ./public --local unix:/run/site.sock

    podnet share [OPTIONS]
        Share files or a local port in a session with a PIN

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --service-url <SERVICE_URL>
            Quick-tunnel provisioning endpoint. Default:
            https://api.trycloudflare.com.

        --user-agent <USER_AGENT>
            User-Agent sent when provisioning

        --ha-connections <HA_CONNECTIONS>
            Edge connections (1-8), for redundancy: when one is lost, the
            others carry the visitors. The edge chooses the connection of each
            request, and one request uses one connection, so more connections
            do not make one transfer faster. Default: ha-connections of
            --config, else 2

        --protocol <PROTOCOL>
            Edge protocol: quic (UDP 7844), http2 or h2 (TCP 7844), or auto
            (quic, then http2). Default: protocol of --config, else auto.
            Values: auto, quic, http2, h2.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            How to reach the edge: auto (try 7844, fall back to WARP on 443),
            direct (port 7844), warp (carried on TCP 443) or relay (HTTP/2 in
            a WebSocket to the relay of --relay, on TCP 443). Default: auto.
            Values: auto, direct, warp, relay.

        --relay <URL>
            The WebSocket-to-TCP relay of --transport relay: a URL, or a comma
            list of hosts of one deployment. The variable PODNET_RELAY_TOKEN
            (not PODNET_RELAY) gives a token; without it, podnet mints one.
            Default: https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev. Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --warp-identity <PATH>
            Keep the WARP device and MASQUE key here and resume them next run.
            Without it, every run registers a new anonymous device

        --leg-failover <LEG_FAILOVER>
            How the next edge leg starts: staggered (when the leg before has
            not registered in 2 s, or at once when it fails) or serial (only
            after the leg before failed). Default: staggered. Values:
            staggered, serial. Variable: PODNET_LEG_FAILOVER.

        --no-verify
            Do not fetch the public URL to prove reachability. Origin TLS
            checks stay on

        --qr
            Print a QR code for the public URL

        --json
            Print the state of the tunnel as JSON lines on stdout, in place of
            the text lines. Each line is one object with the key "event":
            "ready" (url, tunnel_id, locations, and pin for share) or
            "verified" (url)

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C (it also
            ends the verify of the public URL)

        --auth-user <USER>
            Each visitor must give this user (HTTP Basic), with the password
            of --auth-password-file. A visitor with no right credential gets
            401 and reaches no origin; the origin does not get the header. For
            HTTP origins and --forward (podnet connect --auth-user); not for
            --tcp. Variable: PODNET_AUTH_USER.

        --auth-password-file <FILE>
            The file with the password of --auth-user on its first line (mode
            0600). Variable: PODNET_AUTH_PASSWORD_FILE.

        --check
            Check the plan and stop: the flags, the config file, each origin
            (a connection, and the TLS handshake for https, with no request),
            the files and the directories, and the edge legs. No Cloudflare
            API call, no edge connection, no file is written. Exit 0 when each
            check passes, 1 when a check fails. With --json, one JSON document

        --mode <MODE>
            Session mode. With no --mode: download with --file, proxy with
            --port or --unix, upload with --dir. With none of these flags,
            podnet refuses to start: give --mode upload for the default upload
            directory. Values: upload, download, proxy.

        --dir <DIR>
            Directory that receives uploads

        --file <FILE>
            File to share (download mode). A directory goes as one tar stream
            (DIR.tar); names that start with a dot and links out of the
            directory are left out

        --port <PORT>
            Local HTTP port to share (proxy mode)

        --unix <PATH>
            A unix socket of a local HTTP server to share (proxy mode), for a
            host with no TCP listener

        --password
            Require a 6-digit PIN (always on for proxy mode)

        --stop-after
            Stop the tunnel after the first successful transfer

        --idle-secs <IDLE_SECS>
            Stop after this many idle seconds (0 disables). Default: 900.

        --max-request <BYTES>
            Upload mode: the most bytes of one upload request. A larger
            request gets 413 and saves nothing (podnet drops its body). The
            Cloudflare edge accepts at most 100 MB in one request. Default:
            100000000.

        --local <ADDR>
            Serve the session on this local listener and make no tunnel:
            HOST:PORT (or tcp://HOST:PORT), or unix:PATH (mode 0600), as serve
            --local. Not for proxy mode. The tunnel flags have no effect

        --token <TOKEN>
            Named-tunnel token. Prefer the variable TUNNEL_TOKEN or
            --token-file: other users of the host can read a command line.
            Variable: TUNNEL_TOKEN.

        --token-file <PATH>
            Read the named-tunnel token from this file (for example a secret
            of a container). The token is not on the command line. Variable:
            TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Receive files, with a PIN.
            $ podnet share --mode upload --password
        Share an HTTP server on a unix socket, behind a PIN.
            $ podnet share --mode proxy --unix /run/api.sock

    podnet git [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
        Git hosting with the installed git: serve the repositories of a root
        over smart HTTP and SSH, make a repository, print the clone URLs

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Commands of podnet git: serve, init, urls.

    podnet git serve [OPTIONS] --root <DIR>
        Serve the git repositories under a root: smart HTTP on --local,
        through a quick tunnel or both, and SSH on --ssh or through a relay
        pair. It runs the installed git (git http-backend, git upload-pack,
        git receive-pack).

        A fetch needs the read role (--users, or --anon-read), a push needs
        the write role (--push-user, a write user of --users, or a key of
        --authorized-keys). Limits: the quick tunnel takes at most 100 MB in
        one request body, so a larger push over HTTPS fails (a clone has no
        limit); a session through the relay ends at 64 MiB, so a larger clone
        or push through the relay fails.

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --service-url <SERVICE_URL>
            Quick-tunnel provisioning endpoint. Default:
            https://api.trycloudflare.com.

        --user-agent <USER_AGENT>
            User-Agent sent when provisioning

        --ha-connections <HA_CONNECTIONS>
            Edge connections (1-8), for redundancy: when one is lost, the
            others carry the visitors. The edge chooses the connection of each
            request, and one request uses one connection, so more connections
            do not make one transfer faster. Default: ha-connections of
            --config, else 2

        --protocol <PROTOCOL>
            Edge protocol: quic (UDP 7844), http2 or h2 (TCP 7844), or auto
            (quic, then http2). Default: protocol of --config, else auto.
            Values: auto, quic, http2, h2.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            How to reach the edge: auto (try 7844, fall back to WARP on 443),
            direct (port 7844), warp (carried on TCP 443) or relay (HTTP/2 in
            a WebSocket to the relay of --relay, on TCP 443). Default: auto.
            Values: auto, direct, warp, relay.

        --relay <URL>
            The WebSocket-to-TCP relay of --transport relay: a URL, or a comma
            list of hosts of one deployment. The variable PODNET_RELAY_TOKEN
            (not PODNET_RELAY) gives a token; without it, podnet mints one.
            Default: https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev. Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --warp-identity <PATH>
            Keep the WARP device and MASQUE key here and resume them next run.
            Without it, every run registers a new anonymous device

        --leg-failover <LEG_FAILOVER>
            How the next edge leg starts: staggered (when the leg before has
            not registered in 2 s, or at once when it fails) or serial (only
            after the leg before failed). Default: staggered. Values:
            staggered, serial. Variable: PODNET_LEG_FAILOVER.

        --no-verify
            Do not fetch the public URL to prove reachability. Origin TLS
            checks stay on

        --qr
            Print a QR code for the public URL

        --json
            Print the state of the tunnel as JSON lines on stdout, in place of
            the text lines. Each line is one object with the key "event":
            "ready" (url, tunnel_id, locations, and pin for share) or
            "verified" (url)

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C (it also
            ends the verify of the public URL)

        --auth-user <USER>
            Each visitor must give this user (HTTP Basic), with the password
            of --auth-password-file. A visitor with no right credential gets
            401 and reaches no origin; the origin does not get the header. For
            HTTP origins and --forward (podnet connect --auth-user); not for
            --tcp. Variable: PODNET_AUTH_USER.

        --auth-password-file <FILE>
            The file with the password of --auth-user on its first line (mode
            0600). Variable: PODNET_AUTH_PASSWORD_FILE.

        --check
            Check the plan and stop: the flags, the config file, each origin
            (a connection, and the TLS handshake for https, with no request),
            the files and the directories, and the edge legs. No Cloudflare
            API call, no edge connection, no file is written. Exit 0 when each
            check passes, 1 when a check fails. With --json, one JSON document

        --root <DIR>
            The directory that holds the repositories. A request names a
            repository under it (NAME or NAME.git); .. and names that start
            with a dot are refused. Required.

        --local <ADDR>
            Serve smart HTTP on this local listener (more than one is
            permitted): HOST:PORT (or tcp://HOST:PORT), or unix:PATH. Port 0
            takes a free port

        --ssh <LISTEN>
            Serve SSH on HOST:PORT (or tcp://HOST:PORT) or unix:PATH. Only
            ed25519 and ECDSA keys are accepted

        --ingress <INGRESS>
            The road to the clients: tunnel (smart HTTP through a quick
            tunnel; the default with no --local and no --ssh), relay (SSH
            through a relay pair), or none (only --local and --ssh). Values:
            tunnel, relay, none.

        --pair <NAME>
            With --ingress relay: the pair name. Default: the pair with the
            most time left

        --anon-read
            A clone and a fetch need no user and no key (SSH: the user
            anonymous, or a key that is not in --authorized-keys)

        --push-user <USER>
            The user that can push over HTTP (HTTP Basic), with the password
            of --push-password-file

        --push-password-file <FILE>
            The file with the password of --push-user on its first line (mode
            0600)

        --users <FILE>
            The HTTP users, one on each line: USER:ROLE:HASH or
            USER:ROLE:@PASSWORD-FILE, as serve --users. A read user can clone,
            a write user can also push

        --authorized-keys <FILE>
            The keys that can push over SSH (an authorized_keys file)

        --create-on-push
            A push of a write user to a path with no repository makes a bare
            repository there (NAME.git)

        --host-key <FILE>
            The SSH host key (ed25519). podnet makes it one time with mode
            0600. Default: git/ssh_host_ed25519_key in the state directory

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Serve the repositories through a quick tunnel: anyone can clone, the
        user me can push.
            $ podnet git serve --root ./repos --anon-read --push-user me
            --push-password-file ./pass
        Serve the repositories over SSH through a relay pair: ssh -o
        ProxyCommand='podnet relay connect NAME'.
            $ podnet git serve --root ./repos --ingress relay
            --authorized-keys ~/.ssh/authorized_keys

    podnet git init [OPTIONS] --root <DIR> <NAME>
        Make a bare repository NAME under the root (NAME.git when NAME has no
        .git at its end)

        <NAME>
            The path of the new repository under the root (a/b makes
            ROOT/a/b.git). Required.

        --root <DIR>

        --ca-file <PATH>

            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system

    podnet connect [OPTIONS] <REMOTE>
        Bridge a local socket to a remote WebSocket forward endpoint

        <REMOTE>
            Public WebSocket URL, e.g. wss://<host>/__podnet/ws. Required.

        -L, --local <LOCALS>
            Local listeners, repeatable: tcp://[bind:]port or unix:///path. In
            podnet pod with the netns backend, a TCP listener is in the
            network of the pod: use unix:///path to reach it from outside

        --stdio
            Carry one stream on stdin and stdout, with no listener. Use it as
            an SSH ProxyCommand: ssh -o ProxyCommand='podnet connect URL
            --stdio' HOST. podnet exits at the end of the stream. Exit 69: the
            remote does not answer

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C

        --no-check
            Start with no check of the remote. By default, connect opens one
            WebSocket to the remote at start and exits 69 when it fails (the
            origin then dials its forward target once)

        --auth-user <USER>
            The user for a tunnel with --auth-user (HTTP Basic in the
            WebSocket upgrade), with the password of --auth-password-file.
            Variable: PODNET_AUTH_USER.

        --auth-password-file <FILE>
            The file with the password of --auth-user on its first line (mode
            0600). Variable: PODNET_AUTH_PASSWORD_FILE.

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        The client side of --forward.
            $ podnet connect wss://NAME.trycloudflare.com/__podnet/ws -L
            tcp://127.0.0.1:8080

    podnet expose [OPTIONS] <TARGET> [-- <ARGS>...]
        Publish a local service by one word: --via tunnel (a Cloudflare
        tunnel), relay (a node of the reverse relay) or switch (a virtual
        address). It runs `tunnel`, `relay node` or `net proxy --forward`

        <TARGET>
            The local service: an http:// or https:// URL, a port, host:port,
            tcp://host:port, or unix:/path. Required.

        <ARGS>...
            More arguments for the command that runs (after --): for example
            --detach, a pair name or a --switch

        --via <VIA>
            The way to publish it. Default: tunnel. Values: tunnel, relay,
            switch.

        --as <VIRT>
            With --via switch: the virtual address of the service, VIRT as in
            `podnet net proxy --forward VIRT=REAL` (for example
            10.66.0.2:8080)

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet forward [OPTIONS]
        Forward local ports through a network: -L LISTEN=HOST:PORT (TCP, or
        UDP with udp:LISTEN), a DNS door with --dns, with --network SPEC
        (direct, a proxy, the relay, a tailnet)

        -L, --local <LISTEN=HOST:PORT>
            A forward: LISTEN=HOST:PORT (repeatable). LISTEN is PORT (on
            127.0.0.1), ADDR:PORT, tcp://ADDR:PORT or unix:/PATH. Each
            connection to LISTEN goes through the network to HOST:PORT. With
            udp:PORT or udp:ADDR:PORT the forward carries UDP: each client has
            its own flow, and a flow ends after 60 s with no datagram. A
            datagram for a full flow is dropped

        --dns <ADDR:PORT>
            A DNS door: answer DNS queries on ADDR:PORT (UDP and TCP) through
            the network, from the resolver at --dns-upstream

        --dns-upstream <HOST:PORT>
            The resolver of --dns, an address at the far end of the network.
            Default: 1.1.1.1:53.

        --network <SPEC>
            The network of the forwards, as a spec: direct, a proxy URL, relay
            or relay:URL, tailscale:/PATH, unix:/PATH. Default: the way out of
            the process (--proxy, the variables, else direct)

        --run-for <SECONDS>
            Stop after this many seconds

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet route [OPTIONS]
        A router of networks, groups and doors from a config file (--config
        FILE), with health probes and --detach

        --config <FILE>
            The config file of the router: networks, groups, health and doors
            (YAML; podnet man route names the keys)

        --status <unix:/PATH>
            Print the state of a running router: each group and member
            (health, round-trip time, flows), from its control socket (the key
            `control` of its file). Exit 69 when no router answers

        --json
            With --status: print the JSON document

        --check
            Read the file and bring up nothing: exit 0 when it is valid, 64
            with the key that is wrong

        --to <HOST:PORT>
            With --check: a dry run for the target HOST:PORT. Print the rule,
            the network or the group, and the member of each door, with no
            dial. Exit 1 when a door refuses the target or its group has no
            member up

        --door <INDEX>
            With --to: only the door at this position of the file (from 0)

        --run-for <SECONDS>
            Stop after this many seconds

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        --json

    podnet completions [OPTIONS] <SHELL>
        Print a completion script for a shell: bash, zsh, fish, elvish or
        powershell.

        Bash: podnet completions bash >
        ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/podnet. Zsh: podnet
        completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_podnet (with ~/.zfunc in fpath). Fish:
        podnet completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/podnet.fish.
        Elvish: podnet completions elvish > ~/.config/elvish/lib/podnet.elv,
        and use podnet in ~/.config/elvish/rc.elv. PowerShell: podnet
        completions powershell > ~/.config/powershell/podnet.ps1, and .
        ~/.config/powershell/podnet.ps1 in $PROFILE.

        <SHELL>
            Values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh. Required.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet update [OPTIONS]
        Replace this binary with the binary of a release, after checking its
        signature (cosign, release.yml at the tag) and its SHA-256

        --check
            Only say which release is available; change nothing

        --rollback
            Put the binary before the last update (podnet.prev) back, with no
            network. A second --rollback goes forward again

        --force
            Install the release also when it is the version of this binary.
            Without it, podnet says that the version is installed and exits 0

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Say whether a newer release exists. podnet update installs it after it
        checks the cosign signature and the SHA-256.
            $ podnet update --check

    podnet qr [OPTIONS] <URL>
        Print a QR code for a URL

        <URL>

    podnet demo [OPTIONS]
        Test the full path: a built-in origin, a tunnel, a fetch of the URL

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --service-url <SERVICE_URL>
            Quick-tunnel provisioning endpoint. Default:
            https://api.trycloudflare.com.

        --user-agent <USER_AGENT>
            User-Agent sent when provisioning

        --ha-connections <HA_CONNECTIONS>
            Edge connections (1-8), for redundancy: when one is lost, the
            others carry the visitors. The edge chooses the connection of each
            request, and one request uses one connection, so more connections
            do not make one transfer faster. Default: ha-connections of
            --config, else 2

        --protocol <PROTOCOL>
            Edge protocol: quic (UDP 7844), http2 or h2 (TCP 7844), or auto
            (quic, then http2). Default: protocol of --config, else auto.
            Values: auto, quic, http2, h2.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            How to reach the edge: auto (try 7844, fall back to WARP on 443),
            direct (port 7844), warp (carried on TCP 443) or relay (HTTP/2 in
            a WebSocket to the relay of --relay, on TCP 443). Default: auto.
            Values: auto, direct, warp, relay.

        --relay <URL>
            The WebSocket-to-TCP relay of --transport relay: a URL, or a comma
            list of hosts of one deployment. The variable PODNET_RELAY_TOKEN
            (not PODNET_RELAY) gives a token; without it, podnet mints one.
            Default: https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev. Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --warp-identity <PATH>
            Keep the WARP device and MASQUE key here and resume them next run.
            Without it, every run registers a new anonymous device

        --leg-failover <LEG_FAILOVER>
            How the next edge leg starts: staggered (when the leg before has
            not registered in 2 s, or at once when it fails) or serial (only
            after the leg before failed). Default: staggered. Values:
            staggered, serial. Variable: PODNET_LEG_FAILOVER.

        --no-verify
            Do not fetch the public URL to prove reachability. Origin TLS
            checks stay on

        --qr
            Print a QR code for the public URL

        --json
            Print the state of the tunnel as JSON lines on stdout, in place of
            the text lines. Each line is one object with the key "event":
            "ready" (url, tunnel_id, locations, and pin for share) or
            "verified" (url)

        --run-for <RUN_FOR>
            Stay up for this many seconds instead of until Ctrl-C (it also
            ends the verify of the public URL)

        --auth-user <USER>
            Each visitor must give this user (HTTP Basic), with the password
            of --auth-password-file. A visitor with no right credential gets
            401 and reaches no origin; the origin does not get the header. For
            HTTP origins and --forward (podnet connect --auth-user); not for
            --tcp. Variable: PODNET_AUTH_USER.

        --auth-password-file <FILE>
            The file with the password of --auth-user on its first line (mode
            0600). Variable: PODNET_AUTH_PASSWORD_FILE.

        --check
            Check the plan and stop: the flags, the config file, each origin
            (a connection, and the TLS handshake for https, with no request),
            the files and the directories, and the edge legs. No Cloudflare
            API call, no edge connection, no file is written. Exit 0 when each
            check passes, 1 when a check fails. With --json, one JSON document

        --exit-on-verify
            Exit as soon as the public URL has been fetched

        --token <TOKEN>
            Named-tunnel token. Prefer the variable TUNNEL_TOKEN or
            --token-file: other users of the host can read a command line.
            Variable: TUNNEL_TOKEN.

        --token-file <PATH>
            Read the named-tunnel token from this file (for example a secret
            of a container). The token is not on the command line. Variable:
            TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Make a quick tunnel to the built-in origin, and fetch its public URL.
            $ podnet demo --exit-on-verify

    podnet net [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
        Userspace virtual networking (no kernel interfaces)

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Commands of podnet net: demo, doctor, shim, addresses, proxy, switch,
        tailscale, socksify, passwd-shim, ts-shims.

    podnet net demo [OPTIONS]
        Prove the userspace TCP handshake + transfer in-process

        --ca-file <PATH>

            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads

        -q, --quiet

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with

            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each

    podnet net shim [OPTIONS]
        Build (or locate) the LD_PRELOAD shim and print how to use it

        --out <OUT>
            Directory to write and compile the shim into when none is found

        --log
            Log every translation the shim performs

        --map-loopback
            Rewrite 127.0.0.1 connections to the stack's local address

        --map <NAME=ADDR>
            Name-to-address entries for the shim, repeatable: --map
            web=10.66.0.2

        --map-file <PATH>
            Read name entries from a file, repeatable

        --socks-route <ROUTE>
            Send a stream connect to this destination to the SOCKS5 front door
            of --socks-socket, not to the virtual network, repeatable:
            tailnet, ADDR, ADDR/BITS, IPV4:PORT or [IPV6]:PORT

        --socks-socket <PATH>
            The unix socket of the SOCKS5 front door of --socks-route (for
            example of podnet net tailscale). Default: /tmp/podnet-socks.sock.

        --json
            Print the environment as JSON instead of shell assignments

        --ca-file <PATH>

            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system

            Log warnings and errors only

            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority
```
