        --masque-sni <NAME>
            The TLS name of the MASQUE front door in place of
            consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com

        --masque-transport <PROTOCOL>
            The transport of the MASQUE session: h2 (HTTP/2 on TCP 443, the
            default) or h3 (HTTP/3 on UDP 443: each packet is a QUIC datagram;
            no proxy and no relay). Values: h2, h3. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_MASQUE_TRANSPORT.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            The leg of the tunnel: masque (the default) or wireguard (UDP to
            the WireGuard front door, with the device of `podnet warp export`,
            which podnet registers when the file has none). Values: masque,
            wireguard. Variable: PODNET_WARP_TRANSPORT.

        --wireguard-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The WireGuard front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the
            device record (port 2408). Variable: PODNET_WARP_WG_ENDPOINT.

        --carry <CARRY>
            wg: a second WireGuard device inside the tunnel (its own device in
            warp-carry.json of the state directory); the tools use its stack.
            With --transport wireguard, both hops are WireGuard. Values: none,
            wg. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY.

        --carry-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The front door (IP:PORT) of the carried device in place of the one
            of its record. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY_ENDPOINT.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp exec [OPTIONS] <PROGRAM>...
        Run a program under the pod of the running podnet warp up: TCP, DNS
        and UDP go through WARP, also for static binaries. With --detach or
        --name, the pod is an instance (podnet ps, logs, stop): it lives until
        each process of the pod ends, also a daemon that the program started

        <PROGRAM>...
            The program and its arguments. Required.

        -r, --rule <SPEC>
            A podnet-netns rule, repeatable (see podnet pod --help)

        --socket <PATH>
            The socket of the running podnet warp up. Without it:
            PODNET_WARP_SOCKET, warp.sock in the run directory, then the
            pointer file that podnet warp up writes
            ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet/warp-up.json, else podnet-UID in the
            temporary directory)

        --backend <NAME>
            The backend of the pod: auto, netns or seccomp (see podnet pod
            --help). The pod names the backend that runs and its limits in one
            line on stderr; -q removes the line. Default: auto. Values: auto,
            netns, seccomp.

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --join <NAME>
            Run the program in the pod of the instance NAME (warp exec with
            --detach or --name): it reaches the loopback listeners and the
            names of that pod. netns: the program enters the namespaces of the
            pod. seccomp: a new pod shares the inbound listeners and the fake
            DNS table of that pod

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).
            Repeatable; the first that answers wins. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

        --device-name <NAME>
            The name of a new device in the dashboard (1 to 64 characters).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME.

        --device-model <MODEL>
            The model that a new device declares (default PC). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_MODEL.

        --device-locale <LOCALE>
            The locale that a new device declares, as en_US (default en_US).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_LOCALE.

        --fragment-client-hello <MODE>
            Split the TLS ClientHello of the MASQUE connection into records:
            record (records of --fragment-size bytes) or sni (the first record
            ends in the server name). off: one record (the default). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT.

        --fragment-size <MIN[-MAX]>
            The bytes of handshake data in each record of
            --fragment-client-hello: N or MIN-MAX, 16 to 4096 (default
            64-160). Variable: PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT_SIZE.

        --cc <NAME>
            The congestion controller of the TCP connections of the userspace
            stack (what the stack sends): none (the default), reno or cubic.
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_CC.

        --session-max-age <SECS>
            Close each MASQUE session on purpose at this age, and open a new
            one (a new egress address). The TCP flows of the old session end.
            Default: off. Variable: PODNET_WARP_SESSION_MAX_AGE.

        --probe <IP:PORT|off>
            The TCP probe of the data path: IP:PORT or off (default
            1.1.1.1:443). After 3 failed connects (one each 30 s), a new
            session takes the new flows (warp tun: a SYN)

        --no-relay
            Do not try the WebSocket relay (--relay, PODNET_RELAY) when the
            direct MASQUE path fails. Without it, podnet tries the relay: the
            TLS to the front door stays end to end in the WebSocket

        --masque-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The MASQUE front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the device

        --masque-sni <NAME>
            The TLS name of the MASQUE front door in place of
            consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com

        --masque-transport <PROTOCOL>
            The transport of the MASQUE session: h2 (HTTP/2 on TCP 443, the
            default) or h3 (HTTP/3 on UDP 443: each packet is a QUIC datagram;
            no proxy and no relay). Values: h2, h3. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_MASQUE_TRANSPORT.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            The leg of the tunnel: masque (the default) or wireguard (UDP to
            the WireGuard front door, with the device of `podnet warp export`,
            which podnet registers when the file has none). Values: masque,
            wireguard. Variable: PODNET_WARP_TRANSPORT.

        --wireguard-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The WireGuard front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the
            device record (port 2408). Variable: PODNET_WARP_WG_ENDPOINT.

        --carry <CARRY>
            wg: a second WireGuard device inside the tunnel (its own device in
            warp-carry.json of the state directory); the tools use its stack.
            With --transport wireguard, both hops are WireGuard. Values: none,
            wg. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY.

        --carry-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The front door (IP:PORT) of the carried device in place of the one
            of its record. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY_ENDPOINT.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp shell [OPTIONS]
        Run $SHELL under the pod of the running podnet warp up. When it does
        not run, the shell starts as it is (with the proxy variables when the
        env file is there)

        --socket <PATH>
            The socket of the running podnet warp up. Without it:
            PODNET_WARP_SOCKET, warp.sock in the run directory, then the
            pointer file that podnet warp up writes
            ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet/warp-up.json, else podnet-UID in the
            temporary directory)

    podnet warp nc [OPTIONS] <HOST> <PORT>
        A byte pipe from stdin and stdout to HOST:PORT through WARP, for `ssh
        -o ProxyCommand='podnet warp nc %h %p'` and git over SSH. It uses the
        running podnet warp up, else a WARP session of its own

        <HOST>
            Required.

        <PORT>
            Required.

        --socket <PATH>
            The socket of the running podnet warp up. Without it:
            PODNET_WARP_SOCKET, warp.sock in the run directory, then the
            pointer file that podnet warp up writes
            ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet/warp-up.json, else podnet-UID in the
            temporary directory)

        --via-relay
            Go through the WebSocket relay (--relay) to HOST:PORT, with no
            WARP (TCP, IPv4)

        -u, --udp
            UDP: each read of stdin is one datagram to HOST:PORT; each
            datagram that comes back goes to stdout

        --idle <SECS>
            After the end of stdin, end when no data came for this many
            seconds (default 3 with -u, else 5). TCP: podnet then sends the
            FIN

        -N, --shutdown
            TCP: send the FIN at the end of stdin, then wait for the far end
            to close (as nc -N). Without it, podnet sends no FIN until the
            end: some servers drop a half-closed connection before they answer

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).
            Repeatable; the first that answers wins. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME.

        --device-model <MODEL>

            PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_MODEL.

        --fragment-size <MIN[-MAX]>

            --fragment-client-hello: N or MIN-MAX, 16 to 4096 (default

            Log warnings and errors only

            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp ssh-config [OPTIONS]
        Print an SSH config block and GIT_SSH_COMMAND that use podnet warp nc.
        With --write, --remove or --check: own the block in the SSH config
        file, between two marker lines

        --host <HOST>
            The Host pattern of the block (default * for the printed block;
            --write and --check need one)

        --write
            Add the block for --host to the SSH config file, or replace it.
            The block goes before the first Host or Match line. A Host line of
            the file that names the same pattern is an error (exit 1)

        --remove
            Remove the block for --host (with no --host: each block of podnet)

        --check
            Exit 1 when the block for --host is missing or names another
            binary. Writes nothing

        --config <FILE>
            The SSH config file. Default: ~/.ssh/config.

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).
            Repeatable; the first that answers wins. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

        --device-name <NAME>
            The name of a new device in the dashboard (1 to 64 characters).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME.

        --device-model <MODEL>
            The model that a new device declares (default PC). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_MODEL.

        --device-locale <LOCALE>
            The locale that a new device declares, as en_US (default en_US).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_LOCALE.

        --fragment-client-hello <MODE>
            Split the TLS ClientHello of the MASQUE connection into records:
            record (records of --fragment-size bytes) or sni (the first record
            ends in the server name). off: one record (the default). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT.

        --fragment-size <MIN[-MAX]>
            The bytes of handshake data in each record of
            --fragment-client-hello: N or MIN-MAX, 16 to 4096 (default
            64-160). Variable: PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT_SIZE.

        --cc <NAME>
            The congestion controller of the TCP connections of the userspace
            stack (what the stack sends): none (the default), reno or cubic.
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_CC.

        --session-max-age <SECS>
            Close each MASQUE session on purpose at this age, and open a new
            one (a new egress address). The TCP flows of the old session end.
            Default: off. Variable: PODNET_WARP_SESSION_MAX_AGE.

        --probe <IP:PORT|off>
            The TCP probe of the data path: IP:PORT or off (default
            1.1.1.1:443). After 3 failed connects (one each 30 s), a new
            session takes the new flows (warp tun: a SYN)

        --no-relay
            Do not try the WebSocket relay (--relay, PODNET_RELAY) when the
            direct MASQUE path fails. Without it, podnet tries the relay: the
            TLS to the front door stays end to end in the WebSocket

        --masque-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The MASQUE front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the device

        --masque-sni <NAME>
            The TLS name of the MASQUE front door in place of
            consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com

        --masque-transport <PROTOCOL>
            The transport of the MASQUE session: h2 (HTTP/2 on TCP 443, the
            default) or h3 (HTTP/3 on UDP 443: each packet is a QUIC datagram;
            no proxy and no relay). Values: h2, h3. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_MASQUE_TRANSPORT.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            The leg of the tunnel: masque (the default) or wireguard (UDP to
            the WireGuard front door, with the device of `podnet warp export`,
            which podnet registers when the file has none). Values: masque,
            wireguard. Variable: PODNET_WARP_TRANSPORT.

        --wireguard-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The WireGuard front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the
            device record (port 2408). Variable: PODNET_WARP_WG_ENDPOINT.

        --carry <CARRY>
            wg: a second WireGuard device inside the tunnel (its own device in
            warp-carry.json of the state directory); the tools use its stack.
            With --transport wireguard, both hops are WireGuard. Values: none,
            wg. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY.

        --carry-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The front door (IP:PORT) of the carried device in place of the one
            of its record. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY_ENDPOINT.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp tun [OPTIONS]
        Make a TUN interface whose packets go through WARP. Needs
        CAP_NET_ADMIN and /dev/net/tun. Routes are not changed

        --interface <INTERFACE>
            The interface name. Default: podnet0.

        --default-route
            Send the whole host through WARP: host routes keep the MASQUE
            connection outside, default routes go to the TUN (IPv4 and IPv6),
            DNS goes to 1.1.1.1. The default routes go away while the session
            is down; each change is put back at the end

        --keep-rp-filter
            Keep the rp_filter of the interface. Without it, podnet writes 0

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).
            Repeatable; the first that answers wins. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

        --device-name <NAME>
            The name of a new device in the dashboard (1 to 64 characters).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_NAME.

        --device-model <MODEL>
            The model that a new device declares (default PC). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_MODEL.

        --device-locale <LOCALE>
            The locale that a new device declares, as en_US (default en_US).
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_DEVICE_LOCALE.

        --fragment-client-hello <MODE>
            Split the TLS ClientHello of the MASQUE connection into records:
            record (records of --fragment-size bytes) or sni (the first record
            ends in the server name). off: one record (the default). Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT.

        --fragment-size <MIN[-MAX]>
            The bytes of handshake data in each record of
            --fragment-client-hello: N or MIN-MAX, 16 to 4096 (default
            64-160). Variable: PODNET_WARP_FRAGMENT_SIZE.

        --cc <NAME>
            The congestion controller of the TCP connections of the userspace
            stack (what the stack sends): none (the default), reno or cubic.
            Variable: PODNET_WARP_CC.

        --session-max-age <SECS>
            Close each MASQUE session on purpose at this age, and open a new
            one (a new egress address). The TCP flows of the old session end.
            Default: off. Variable: PODNET_WARP_SESSION_MAX_AGE.

        --probe <IP:PORT|off>
            The TCP probe of the data path: IP:PORT or off (default
            1.1.1.1:443). After 3 failed connects (one each 30 s), a new
            session takes the new flows (warp tun: a SYN)

        --no-relay
            Do not try the WebSocket relay (--relay, PODNET_RELAY) when the
            direct MASQUE path fails. Without it, podnet tries the relay: the
            TLS to the front door stays end to end in the WebSocket

        --masque-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The MASQUE front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the device

        --masque-sni <NAME>
            The TLS name of the MASQUE front door in place of
            consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com

        --masque-transport <PROTOCOL>
            The transport of the MASQUE session: h2 (HTTP/2 on TCP 443, the
            default) or h3 (HTTP/3 on UDP 443: each packet is a QUIC datagram;
            no proxy and no relay). Values: h2, h3. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_MASQUE_TRANSPORT.

        --transport <TRANSPORT>
            The leg of the tunnel: masque (the default) or wireguard (UDP to
            the WireGuard front door, with the device of `podnet warp export`,
            which podnet registers when the file has none). Values: masque,
            wireguard. Variable: PODNET_WARP_TRANSPORT.

        --wireguard-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The WireGuard front door (IP:PORT) in place of the one of the
            device record (port 2408). Variable: PODNET_WARP_WG_ENDPOINT.

        --carry <CARRY>
            wg: a second WireGuard device inside the tunnel (its own device in
            warp-carry.json of the state directory); the tools use its stack.
            With --transport wireguard, both hops are WireGuard. Values: none,
            wg. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY.

        --carry-endpoint <IP:PORT>
            The front door (IP:PORT) of the carried device in place of the one
            of its record. Variable: PODNET_WARP_CARRY_ENDPOINT.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,

            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:

            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet warp run [OPTIONS] <PROGRAM>...
        Run a program with all its traffic sent through WARP. No root and no
        TUN device are necessary (podnet-netns)

        <PROGRAM>...
            The program and its arguments. Required.

        --backend <BACKEND>
            The backend: auto, netns-raw, netns or seccomp. netns-raw moves
            the raw packets of a namespace through WARP (TCP, UDP, ICMP, IPv6;
            no root). auto takes netns-raw when it works, else seccomp, so
            that UDP goes through WARP too. Default: auto.

        -r, --rule <SPEC>
            A podnet-netns rule, repeatable: domain:NAME=PROXY,
            domain:.SUFFIX=PROXY, cidr:NET/LEN=PROXY; PROXY may be direct

        --keep-proxy-env
            The program keeps the proxy variables of this shell

        --inbound-dir <DIR>
            Where a port that the program listens on is a unix socket (seccomp
            backend). The directory must be of this user and not writable by
            the group or others [default:
            $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet-netns-inbound, else
            $TMPDIR/podnet-netns-inbound-UID]

        --identity <PATH>
            The file that keeps the device and its MASQUE key, so that each
            run uses the same device. Default: warp.json in the state
            directory (see PODNET_STATE_DIR in podnet man environment)

        --ephemeral
            Register a new device for this run only, and do not save it

        --resolver <SPEC>
            A resolver of the DNS inside the tunnel, in place of 1.1.1.1:53:
            IP[:PORT] (UDP), or tls://IP[:PORT][#NAME] (DNS over TLS, port
            853; the certificate must have NAME, or the IP address).
            Repeatable; the first that answers wins. Variable:
            PODNET_WARP_RESOLVERS.

            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Run a program with its traffic through WARP.
            $ podnet warp run -- curl https://www.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace

    podnet relay [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
        Inbound access to this host through the WebSocket relay (--relay):
        pair, run a node for a local port, connect as the operator

        --relay <URL>
            The relay for a new pair. A pair keeps the relay that made it.
            Default: https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev. Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Commands of podnet relay: pair, node, connect, stop.

    podnet relay pair [OPTIONS]
        Ask the relay for a pair: a name, a node token (kept in a file of mode
        0600 in the state directory) and a connect token for the operator. A
        pair lasts at most 72 h

        --json
            Print the pair as JSON (with the connect token, not the node
            token)

        --relay <URL>
            The relay for a new pair. A pair keeps the relay that made it.
            Default: https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev. Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Ask the relay for a pair: a name, and the tokens of the node and of
        the operator.
            $ podnet relay pair

    podnet relay node [OPTIONS] --to <TARGET> [PAIR]
        Hold the node socket of a pair, and connect each session of an
        operator to a local service. A lost socket is opened again

        <PAIR>
            The pair name. Default: the pair with the most time left

        --to <TARGET>
            The local service: host:port or unix:/path. Required.

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>
            The name of the detached instance. Default: the command and a hash
            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this
            process under the name (it is not forked and not restarted);
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>
            With --detach: seconds to wait for the instance to be ready (else
            exit 124). Default: 60.

        --replace
            Stop a running instance of the same name that has other arguments,
            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix
            socket of -L that another process serves (by default, a socket
            that answers is refused, exit 69; a stale socket file is replaced)

        --no-restart
            Do not start the instance again when it ends. Without it, a
            supervisor starts it again with a backoff (1 s to 30 s), but not
            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,
            --idle-secs, --run-for). A quick tunnel gets a new URL; podnet ps
            shows it. With --name and no --detach, there is no supervisor

        --relay <URL>
            The relay for a new pair. A pair keeps the relay that made it.
            Default: https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev. Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Give the SSH server of this host to the operators of the pair, through
        the relay.
            $ podnet relay node --to 127.0.0.1:22

    podnet relay connect [OPTIONS] <NAME>
        Open a session to a node and copy stdin and stdout (an SSH
        ProxyCommand), or each connection of --listen

        <NAME>
            The pair name. Required.

        --token <TOKEN>
            The connect token. Prefer the variable or --token-file: other
            users of the host can read a command line. Default: the local pair
            file. Variable: PODNET_RELAY_CONNECT_TOKEN.

        --token-file <PATH>
            Read the connect token from this file

        --listen <LISTEN>
            Accept local connections here (tcp://[bind:]port or unix:/path),
            one session for each, in place of stdin and stdout

        --detach
            Run in the background: podnet prints one JSON document when the
            command is ready (its URL or its listen address) and exits 0. The
            instance keeps running when the shell or the terminal closes.
            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop manage it

        --name <NAME>

            of its arguments. A second start with the same name and the same
            arguments gives the same instance. With no --detach: register this

            podnet ps, logs, wait and stop see it

        --ready-timeout <SECS>

            exit 124). Default: 60.

            and start this one (needs --detach). connect: also take a unix

            after exit 64 or 78, and not after a planned end (--stop-after,

        --relay <URL>

            Default: https://tcp.ssh.relay.ajam.dev. Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each

            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy

        --egress <SPEC>

            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and

            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet relay stop [OPTIONS] <NAME>

        the local pair file

        --relay <URL>

    podnet pod [OPTIONS] [ARGS]...
        Run a program with all its traffic sent through a proxy
        (podnet-netns).

        Give the podnet-netns arguments after `pod`. See `podnet pod --help`.
        podnet gives the line after `pod` to podnet-netns: the global options
        of podnet (-q, -v, --color, --log-format) do not apply to it.

        Run a program with all egress through a proxy, without shims

        Usage: podnet pod [OPTIONS] -- <PROGRAM> [ARGS]...
               podnet pod doctor [--json]
               podnet pod --serve <LISTEN> -x <PROXY>

        Arguments:
          <PROGRAM> [ARGS]... The program to run, and its arguments

        Options:
          -x, --proxy <SPEC> Upstream proxy, repeatable; more than one chains:
                                     socks5://[user:pass@]host:port
                                     http://[user:pass@]host:port
                                     socks5://unix:/path (unix-socket proxy)
                                     http://unix:/path (HTTP CONNECT on a unix
                                     socket)
                                     socks5h+unix:/path, http+unix:/path (the
                                     same)
                                     tailscale:/path/to/tailscaled.sock
                                   Default: $ALL_PROXY, $HTTPS_PROXY or
                                   $HTTP_PROXY.
                                   --egress SPEC is the same option (its name
                                   in each
                                   podnet command)
          -r, --rule <SPEC> Per-destination route; first match wins:
                                     domain:NAME=socks5://host:port
                                     domain:.example.com=... (the name and
                                     each
                                                               name under it)
                                     cidr:10.0.0.0/8=socks5://host:port
                                     cidr:10.0.0.0/8=direct (no proxy)
                                     domain:.ads.example=reject (refuse; also
                                     block):
                                     connect fails with ECONNREFUSED (netns: a
                                     RST),
                                     a datagram with EACCES (netns: dropped),
                                     --serve answers SOCKS5 0x02 or HTTP 403
                                   With the seccomp backend, 127.0.0.0/8 goes
                                   direct
                                   (or to a listener of the program itself)
              --allow-shadowed-rules
                                   A rule that an earlier rule shadows (it can
                                   never
                                   match) gives a warning. A shadowed reject
                                   rule is
                                   an error (exit 64); this option makes it a
                                   warning
              --default-action <A> allow (default) or reject: what the pod
              does with a
                                   target that no rule matches. reject refuses
                                   it as
                                   a reject rule does
              --loopback-rules Seccomp backend: apply the rules to a TCP
              connect to
                                   127.0.0.0/8 and ::1 (by default it goes
                                   direct). A
                                   refused one gets ECONNREFUSED; an allowed
                                   one goes
                                   direct
              --flow-log <FILE> Append one JSON line to FILE for each decision
                                   (time, target, rule or default, chain,
                                   verdict)
                                   and one at the close of each relayed TCP
                                   flow
                                   (bytes_out, bytes_in)
              --learn <FILE> Write each destination of the run to FILE, one
                                   PROTO TARGET line each. A flow that a rule
                                   refuses goes through the -x chain
              --fail-on-violation <FILE>
                                   Refuse each destination that is not in FILE
                                   (a
                                   file of --learn). A learned destination
                                   that a
                                   rule refuses is also a violation. The pod
                                   writes
                                   each violation on stderr and exits 4 when
                                   the
                                   program exits 0
              --flow-budget <N> Seccomp backend: the most sockets of the
              program
                                   that the pod tracks at one time (64 to
                                   1048576).
                                   A socket call above it gets EMFILE.
                                   Default: from
                                   RLIMIT_NOFILE (pod doctor shows it)
              --map <NAME=ADDR> Resolve NAME to ADDR locally, repeatable
              --keep-proxy-env Keep HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, ALL_PROXY and
              NO_PROXY
                                   (and the lower-case forms) for the program;
                                   by
                                   default the program does not get them
              --backend <NAME> auto (default), netns or seccomp. With netns, a
                                   listener of the program is in the network
                                   of the
                                   pod: a loopback TCP listener is not seen
                                   from
                                   outside; use a unix socket (connect -L
                                   unix:///PATH)
              --prefer-udp With auto: seccomp first when it works (UDP
                                   datagrams of any size go through; netns
                                   carries
                                   a datagram of 1500 bytes at most)
              --name-backend Print one line on stderr that names the backend
                                   that runs, its limits and the reason of the
                                   choice (also after auto)
              --inbound-dir <DIR> Where a bound port is exposed as a unix
              socket
                                   (seccomp backend only). The directory must
                                   be of
                                   this user and not writable by the group or
                                   by
                                   others; a new one gets mode 0700
                                   [default:
                                   $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podnet-netns-inbound,
                                   else $TMPDIR/podnet-netns-inbound-UID]
              --host-gateway Netns backend: a TCP connect to the gateway of
              the
                                   pod (10.66.255.254) and a port goes to
                                   127.0.0.1
                                   and that port on the host; a UDP datagram
                                   to the
                                   gateway (not port 53) goes from a UDP
                                   socket of
                                   the host. Off by default: the connect is
                                   refused
              --session <DIR> Seccomp backend: share the inbound listeners
                                   (DIR/inbound, unless --inbound-dir) and the
                                   fake
                                   DNS table (DIR/dns) with each pod of DIR.
                                   The
                                   directory must be of this user and not
                                   writable
                                   by the group or by others. The netns
                                   backend does
                                   not use it
              --serve <LISTEN> Serve SOCKS5, HTTP CONNECT and UDP ASSOCIATE on
                                   unix:/path or tcp://host:port, forwarding
                                   through
                                   the -x chain
          -v, --verbose Log each flow; with seccomp, also each socket and
                                   each setsockopt that the pod emulates
          -V, --version Print the version
          -h, --help Print help

        Exit status: the exit code of the program; 64 for a usage mistake
        (also no
        proxy at all); 3 when no backend can run on this host; 4 for a
        violation of
        --fail-on-violation when the program exits 0. The pod returns when
        the program exits; a process that the program started keeps the
        network of
        the pod until it exits. doctor measures what
        the host permits and exits 3 when no backend can run.


        <ARGS>...
            The podnet-netns arguments

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Run a program with all its traffic through a proxy.
            $ podnet pod -x socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 -- curl
            https://example.com

    podnet man [OPTIONS] [SECTION]...
        Show the manual, generated from this binary

        <SECTION>...

            gives both

        --no-pager

        --roff

        --json

        --ca-file <PATH>

            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads

        Examples:

        Examples:

            $ podnet status

    podnet doctor [OPTIONS]
        Test the path from this host to the edge: the proxy, TCP and TLS to
        the APIs, the edge (7844) and MASQUE (443), and UDP 7844. Exit 0 when
        at least one leg (quic, http2, quic+warp) can work, 1 when none can

        --json
            Print one JSON document

        --quick
            A short run: one sample for each path, and 15 s for the whole run.
            A part that does not end in time gets the verdict `unknown`. The
            JSON document keeps the same keys

        --agent
            Test what dev work can do here: git over HTTPS and SSH, the
            package registries, UDP DNS, IPv6 and localhost, directly, through
            the proxy and through a running podnet warp up; then print the
            commands to run

        --samples <SAMPLES>
            Samples of each TCP path (1-9). All samples end in 10 s. Default:
            9.

        --timeout <TIMEOUT>
            The time limit of one connection and of one TLS handshake, in
            seconds. Default: 3.

        --relay <URL>
            The relay to test, as the `--relay` of `tunnel` (a loopback
            `http://` relay is allowed). Variable: PODNET_RELAY.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        Test the path from this host to the edge; the last line names the step
        to take.
            $ podnet doctor

    podnet autostart [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
        Start a podnet command at boot, with no root: a systemd user unit (it
        stops at logout unless linger is on), else an @reboot line in the
        crontab

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Commands of podnet autostart: add, remove, list, run.

    podnet autostart add [OPTIONS] <NAME> [-- <ARGS>...]
        Add an entry that runs `podnet ARGS`. The token and a proxy password
        go to a private env file (mode 0600), not to the unit, the crontab or
        the command line. Exit 69 when this host has no systemd user manager
        and no crontab

        <NAME>
            The name of the entry (letters, digits, - and _). Required.

        <ARGS>...
            The podnet command and its arguments, after `--`, with no leading
            `podnet` (one is dropped). The command must parse

        --from <INSTANCE>
            Take the command and its arguments from the detached instance
            INSTANCE (podnet ps), with no --detach options

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>

            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:

        --no-proxy

        --egress <SPEC>

            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet autostart run [OPTIONS] --dir <DIR> <NAME>

    podnet agent [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
        One command for a sandbox with basic networking: test what works,
        start WARP when it is needed, expose ports, and print what works now
        and the commands to use

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://

            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand

            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the

            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>

            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the

            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Commands of podnet agent: up, down, status.

    podnet agent up [OPTIONS]
        Test the host (podnet doctor --agent), start podnet warp up when
        direct networking does not do each task, start a detached quick tunnel
        for each --expose PORT, and print one JSON document

        --persist
            Also add the block of podnet warp up --persist to the shell files

        --expose <PORT>
            A local port to expose with a quick tunnel (repeatable)

        --port <PORT>
            The TCP port of the WARP proxy on 127.0.0.1. Default: 40000.

        --warp
            Start WARP also when direct networking works

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

        Examples:
        In a sandbox: test what works, start WARP when it is needed, and print
        the commands to use.
            $ podnet agent up

    podnet agent down [OPTIONS]
        Stop what podnet agent up started and put back each change

        Examples:

    podnet stop [OPTIONS] <NAME|--all>
        Stop a detached instance: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after --timeout

        <NAME>
            The name of the instance (podnet ps)

        --all
            Stop each instance

        --timeout <TIMEOUT>
            Seconds to wait before SIGKILL. Default: 10.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,

            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet logs [OPTIONS] <NAME>
        Print the log of a detached instance

        <NAME>
            The name of the instance (podnet ps). Required.

        -f, --follow
            Print new lines as they come, until Ctrl-C

        -n, --lines <LINES>
            Print only the last lines

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

    podnet wait [OPTIONS] <NAME>
        Wait until a detached instance is ready, and print its ready document

        <NAME>
            The name of the instance (podnet ps). Required.

        --timeout <TIMEOUT>
            Seconds to wait (else exit 69). Default: 60.

        --ca-file <PATH>
            A file of TLS roots (PEM). podnet uses only these roots for each
            connection that it opens as a client. Without it, podnet reads
            SSL_CERT_FILE, else podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the system
            bundle and the compiled-in roots

        --proxy <URL>
            The proxy for each connection: http://, socks5:// or socks5h://
            [user:password@]host[:port]. A proxy on a unix socket:
            socks5h+unix:/PATH (or socks5h://unix:/PATH). A proxy at the stdin
            and stdout of a command, one for each connection (as ProxyCommand
            of SSH): http+exec:COMMAND or socks5h+exec:COMMAND. Without it,
            podnet reads HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY (no +exec: there). NO_PROXY
            names the targets that do not use a proxy. PODNET_PROXY gives the
            same value, and keeps a password out of the command line.
            Percent-encode / ? # @ : in the user and the password. Variable:
            PODNET_PROXY.

        --no-proxy
            Use no proxy, also when HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY is set

        --egress <SPEC>
            The way out, as a network spec: direct (as --no-proxy), a proxy
            URL (as --proxy), relay or relay:URL (as --transport relay and
            --relay). With podnet pod, each --egress is one -x hop of the
            chain, in its order (also tailscale:/PATH and unix:/PATH)

        --resolve <HOST=IP>
            Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP].
            PODNET_RESOLVE adds to it. TLS still checks the name of the
            certificate

        -q, --quiet
            Log warnings and errors only

        -v, --verbose
            Log more: -v for debug, -vv for trace. RUST_LOG takes priority

        --color <COLOR>
            Colours in the log: auto (only on a terminal, and not with
            NO_COLOR), always or never. Default: auto. Values: auto, always,
            never.

        --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
            The form of the log on stderr: text, or json (one object for each
            line). Default: text. Values: text, json.

ENVIRONMENT
    HTTPS_PROXY, https_proxy, ALL_PROXY, all_proxy
        The proxy for each connection of podnet, when --proxy and --no-proxy
        are not given: http://, socks5:// (this host resolves the name) or
        socks5h:// (the proxy resolves it), [user:password@]host[:port]. The
        first variable that is set and can be parsed is used. With a proxy,
        --protocol auto does not try QUIC on UDP 7844. podnet pod uses the
        value as its default upstream. (tunnel, warp, edge discovery, pod)
    NO_PROXY, no_proxy
        The targets that do not use the proxy, separated by commas: * (all), a
        name (it matches the names under it too), .name, an IP address, a
        network (10.0.0.0/8), each with an optional :port. (all commands)
    PODNET_RESOLVE
        Addresses for names, in place of DNS: HOST=IP[,HOST=IP]. --resolve
        adds to it. Without a pin, podnet asks the system resolver, then DNS
        over HTTPS at 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1, 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4. A bad value is a
        configuration error (exit 78) for each command. (all commands)
    PODNET_TAILNET
        The tailnet that tailscaled must run in, in place of --tailnet: the
        name or the DNS suffix. The door starts only when the daemon is
        Running in it, and refuses new dials when the daemon changes to
        another tailnet. (net tailscale)
    TS_FORCE_NOISE_443
        Read only, to show its value in the tailscaled row of net doctor. It
        is a variable of tailscaled: set it to true when tailscaled starts on
        a host that reaches only port 443 (the control connection tries port
        80 first). (net doctor)
    HTTP_PROXY, http_proxy
        The default upstream of podnet pod when HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY are
        not set. (pod)
    TUNNEL_TOKEN
        The named-tunnel token, in place of --token. Other users of the host
        can read a command line, but not the environment of a process of
        another user. (tunnel, serve, share, demo)
    TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE
        A file with the named-tunnel token, in place of --token-file.
        TUNNEL_TOKEN wins when both are set. An empty file is a usage error
        (exit 64). (tunnel, serve, share, demo)
    SSL_CERT_FILE
        The only file of TLS roots (PEM), when --ca-file is not given. Without
        both, podnet trusts podnet-ca.pem beside the binary, the first system
        bundle that it can read, and the roots compiled into podnet. (all
        commands)
